items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Had Orville Harris on alto, Andy Brown on alto and Walter Thomas on tenor.

ctx.x: No, I was going to ask you.

Well, there was me, I was the added saxophone. Had Orville Harris on alto, Andy Brown on alto and Walter Thomas on tenor. Then they had Lamar Wright on trumpet, Doc Cheetham on trumpet and Edwin Swazey on trumpet. Then they had De Priest Wheeler on trombone and Harry White

on trombone. And Benny Payne was on piano, Al Morgan on bass, Maurice White on guitar and Leroy Maxey on drums. And then later when Edwin Swazey died Irving Randolph took his place. And then later on Keg (DOMESTIC) Johnson came in the band in Harry White's place. And then we added another trombone which was Claude Jones. And then Ben Webster took Orville Harris' place so we had two tenors and two altos then. And that's how the band was when I left the band in '35.

items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: So it just so happened that Eddie Barefield had that letter, and we took the letter down to the union -- and I went with him.

ctx.x: So it just so happened that Eddie Barefield had that letter, and we took the letter down to the union -- and I went with him. Because Cab didn't have time to do all that shit. But see, I got to the place that he just let me run the band, and I ran it with the best of my knowledge. So I went down to the union, and I told them, I said, 'We've got this guy on the road and he's got this letter that says that he wants to be in the union, wherever he is...'
